The killing involved several roles that should not be collapsed into one name. Katangan authorities executed Lumumba, Belgian officers took part and Belgian government actions contributed to his removal and transfer. The commission's finding addresses moral responsibility for the circumstances leading to death. These parts can be explained together without inventing a written order from every participating institution. Conversely, the absence of such an order from the finding would not erase the roles that are documented. A precise account recognizes the specific kinds of involvement instead of requiring one totalizing attribution before it can acknowledge that Belgium played a part in the events ending in the execution.

A poisoning plot by the CIA belongs to a different proposed mechanism from the execution that occurred in Katanga. The plan demonstrates a real intention within that separate history, but it did not directly carry out the killing described here. Treating every hostile plan as the cause of the eventual death would lose the distinction between proposal, assistance, transfer and execution. The Belgian parliamentary inquiry and later apology concern Belgian responsibility in the actual chain of events. They can be discussed alongside the separate CIA plot, provided that each retains its own evidential and causal scope rather than one genuine plot being used to substitute a different perpetrator for the recorded killing.

The source connects the commission to removal, transfer and the conditions of the killing, while the officers' participation concerns the event itself. The CIA plotted to poison Lumumba but did not directly carry out the killing described here. The source allows mention of that separate plot while rejecting a CIA-perpetrator account. A collision prediction needs an observed object and an orbit from which a future encounter can be inferred. The Nibiru story instead asks for the final prediction while treating the object's existence as already settled. Without the established object and trajectory, a date would be an invented endpoint rather than an astronomical result. This is different from uncertainty in a measurement of a real known body. The doomsday premise itself is unsupported. NASA's account also notes that a threatening object of the claimed scale would have been visible to astronomers well before the proposed collision, rather than available only through a hidden timetable controlled by one institution.

The names Planet X, Planet Nine and Nibiru can be used loosely in popular stories, but names do not identify the same object or the same claim. A distant unobserved planetary hypothesis does not carry the alleged approaching trajectory or doomsday purpose of Nibiru. Likewise, a real dwarf planet such as Eris does not become an undisclosed threat by being discussed in the same conversation. Distinguishing the propositions prevents ordinary astronomical uncertainty from being borrowed to support a different collision scenario. The unresolved parts of a separate hypothesis do not establish the particular threatening planet or justify presenting a future strike as an event expected to happen to Earth.
